messages.author: 177d6b42224d530a
messages.subject: Identification issue with formative construct
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to run a  model with a formative construct (called OVA) for the first time. Unfortunately I got the following message

Warning message:
lavaan->lav_model_vcov():  
   Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could not be inverted. This may be a  symptom that the model is not identified. 

I do not understand why the model is not identified nor how to identify it.

I looked at previous discussions on the google group on this topic where it was explained that one need to manually fix some of the parameters to known non-zero values to identify the model.

As a consequence I fixed one path regression to 1 (1*COG) to identify it and it yields the above message of error. In addition I also try to fix the variance of the formative variable to 1 (OVA ~~ 1*OVA) but It did not solve the problem. 

Can anyone help me ?

model_ovr <- '
PCV =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4
PIG =~ V5 + V6 + V7
PHS =~ V8 + V9 + V10 +V11
PIT =~ V12 + V13 + V14 + V15
PAD =~ V16 + V17 + V18
PAN =~ V19 + V20 + V21
PAA =~ V22 + V23+ V24
COG =~ PCV + PIG + PHS + PIT + PAD + PAN + PAA
PCV ~~ 1*PCV
PIG ~~ 1*PIG
PHS ~~ 1*PHS
PIT ~~ 1*PIT
PAD ~~ 1*PAD
PAN ~~ 1*PAN
PAA ~~ 1*PAA
COG ~~ 1*COG

PAF =~ V25 + V26 + V27 + V28
PAF ~~ 1*PAF

OVA <~  1*COG + PAF

'

fit_ovr <- cfa(model_ovr, data = TOUR)
summary(fit_ovr, fit.measures =TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Identification issue with formative construct
parts:
Pierre-Charles--
     Here is a similar problem. You want to fill a paper bag with apples and pears. How many apples and how many pears will it take to fill the bag? There is not one specific number of apples or pears because each depends on the other. And, in this case, we don't even know the size of the bag.
     Fixing the variances of the component factors to 1 does not change the problem--lavaan's default of fixing a loading to 1 would have worked just as well. Here, you fix one of the weights to 1 but that leaves free (1) the variance of OVA and (2) the weight for PAF. The variance of OVA is unknown and so are its covariances with everything else in the model.
     To make OVA the sum of two variables, you must fix OVA's residual variance to 0. OVA ~~0*OVA
     For the model to be identified, there must be constraints on OVA in terms of other model variables. Mostly, OVA must do something--predict something, so that there can be a better or worse value for OVA's variance and its covariances with other variables in the model. If you constrain OVA's covariances with the other variables, that would start to give the bag some shape. With OVA's residual variance fixed to 0, you could force the two weights to equality, but even then...how big is the bag? The higher the weights, the larger OVA's variance, even if its residual variance is constrained to 0.

parts:
Professor Rigdon,

Thank you very much for your helpful reply and the time taken to reply.

Firstly, you mentioned "Here is a similar problem". So I perhaps miss a discussion on the topic.

Secondly, I have in fact I have a more general model in which OVA predicts another construct (LOY).

In this more general model, however, when I fixed OVA residual variance to 0 I also have problem of identification. As a consequence I fixed the regression path of OVA to LOY (LOY  ~ 1*OVA) in order to achieve identification but it also does not work.


## Fit the GLOBAL model

model_g <- '

PCV =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4
PIG =~ V5 + V6 + V7
PHS =~ V8 + V9 + V10 + V11
PIT =~ V12 + V13 + V14 + V15
PAD =~ V16 + V17 + V18
PAN =~ V19 + V20 + V21

COG =~ PCV + PIG + PHS + PIT + PAD + PAN + PAA
PCV ~~ 1*PCV
PIG ~~ 1*PIG
PHS ~~ 1*PHS
PIT ~~ 1*PIT
PAD ~~ 1*PAD
PAN ~~ 1*PAN
PAA ~~ 1*PAA
COG ~~ 1*COG


PAF =~ V25 + V26 + V27 + V28
PAF ~~ 1*PAF

OVA <~ 1*COG + PAF

OVA ~~0*OVA

IRF =~ V29 + V30 + V31 + V32
IRE =~ V33 + V34 + V35
LOY =~ IRF + IRE

IRF ~~ 1*IRF
IRE ~~ 1*IRE
LOY ~~ 1*LOY


PAF ~ COG

LOY ~ COG

LOY ~ PAF

LOY  ~ 1*OVA

'

fit_model <- cfa(model_g, data = TOUR)
summary(fit_model, fit.measures =TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Identification issue with formative construct
parts:
Pierre-Charles--
     In this model you have COG and PAF forming OVA, and then OVA predicting LOY, but you also have COG and PAF predicting LOY. But those direct effects mean that OVA, intended as a composite of COG and PAF, has nothing to contribute to predicting LOY. Put another way, OVA must be perfectly collinear with COG and PAF, so the regression of LOY on OVA, COG and PAF must fail.
     If OVA were, say, an interaction term, then your model could be asking whether there is some nonlinear effect of COG and PAF on LOY, but you would specify the model differently.
     Even without the direct effects from COG and PAF to LOY, it would be difficult for a composite OVA to add anything to the model. Compare two models:
1. COG + PAF predict LOY directly, without an OVA
2. COG and PAF predict OVA, which predicts LOY
Even with constraints such as you have applied here, the first model has 2 parameters of interest--the regression weights for COG and PAF predicting LOY. The second model also has two paths of interest--the regression of OVA on PAF and the regression of LOY on OVA. (Both models also include the free residual variance of LOY.) The two models are going to be roughly equivalent, with just a translation of parameter values. There may be some circumstances where including the extra variable OVA could induce lack of fit based on violating assumed 0 residual covariances with other variables in the model. But given the structure of your model, I don't see an opportunity for that. So I think the best you can achieve is equality between the two models--same fit, same degrees of freedom, and same R2 for the LOY variable.
     There might be a reason to want to capture the value of the weighted sum of COG and PAFm as defined by the factor model, but I don't think this is the way to do it. You might create a new parameter to capture this--a parameter that is a specific function of other parameters. But here I am taking you down a different path.
